Subject: SIG — Physical Media Refresh Plan and Support Escalation Flow

Tom / Acme team,

Thanks again for walking through the SIG items yesterday. A few follow-ups from our side to make the on-prem / air-gapped addendum operational:

1) Physical media refresh cadence — we proposed quarterly image + patch bundles shipped on encrypted USB by default; annual full-image courier option for major upgrades.
2) Delivery options — insured courier vs. sealed hand-delivery. We can support both; courier manifest and chain-of-custody will be included.
3) Update installation guide — short on-site checklist for your infra team and SCP/rsync instructions for teams that prefer mounted transfer.
4) Support & escalation — suggested 24x5 M-F first-response SLA for on-call during a refresh window, with an on-site dispatch option for critical failures.

Attached: media_manifest_v1.csv (sample manifest), scp_instructions.pdf (transfer + verification steps), support_escalation_matrix.xlsx (proposed RACI and SLAs).

Can you confirm: a) preferred delivery method (courier vs hand-delivery), b) any customs/clearing requirements we should know about, and c) whether Acme wants Redwood staff present for the initial refresh?

If that looks good I'll schedule a short walkthrough with Marcus (logistics) and Evelyn (support ops) for next week.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Stephanie,

Appreciate the summary. A few notes from Acme side:

- Delivery: we prefer insured courier for quarterly bundles; for major upgrades we'd like the hand-delivery option but must pre-clear personnel with our security ops team.
- Customs / import: nothing special for US domestic deliveries, but for EU-based subsidiaries we need CN22/Customs pack and a local contact.
- On-site presence: OK for the first planned refresh; security requires a two-week notice and a completed background check form for any Redwood person on site.

One question: will the delivered media include checksums and an optional signed manifest? We need to anchor the chain-of-custody to a verifiable signature on receipt.

Tom
Tom Reilly
Director, Information Security
Acme Financial

Tom / team — following up with the logistics and technical details: 

- Checksums & signed manifest: yes. We will provide SHA256 checksums for each artifact and a PGP-signed manifest file. Manifest includes artifact UUID, build tag, sequence number, and expiry.
- Chain-of-custody: courier manifest + tamper-evident seals. For hand-delivery we will provide ID + company badge copies (redacted per privacy policy) ahead of arrival.
- Transfer options: default is encrypted USB (LUKS) + verified mount instructions. For sites that prefer direct block-level transfer via physically-connected host, we will provide scp/rsync over an isolated transfer node and verify with checksums.
- Support model: proposed SLOs in support_escalation_matrix.xlsx: 2-hour P1 initial response during refresh window, 24-hour P2, next-business-day P3. On-site dispatch within 48 hours for P1 if agreed in statement of work.

I've attached an updated manifest (media_manifest_v1.csv) with placeholder shipment IDs. Evelyn, can you confirm the staffing plan and whether we should include a local vendor option for EU shipments?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Logistics
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachments: media_manifest_v1.csv
